units.titles: The Oracle Aggregator Can Be Hijacked By Third-Parties
units.known_address_notes: Runtime Verification 2024-12 audited ClickPesa Debt Fund's fork of Blend's Soroban Oracle Aggregator (commit e57d0607). The report (Jina text) contains no contract ID; the repo publishes none; Blend's mainnet deployment table has no ClickPesa entry; stellar.expert search for 'clickpesa'/'oracle-aggregator' returns no contract. Core lending pool is live per the report, but the audited oracle contract ID is unpublished.

units.titles: [H-01] Swapper.sol::Swap - No slippage control on token swap.
units.known_address_notes: Hashlock report states network=ARBITRUM, platform Arbitrum/Solidity, audited commit 5f4cb3a5df264383ca8704c069469a3610066fcd; scope is a perp-trading stack (Swapper.sol, AccountProxy.sol/Account.sol, Exchange.sol). Code delivered via private GitHub. No addresses in the report; no deployment/address page found for the DVX app (searches returned unrelated Arbitrum DEXes). -> PARTIAL.

units.project: Dapper Labs Dapper Smart Contract Wallet
units.titles: Replay Attacks on Co-signer Signed Invocations
units.known_address_notes: The published Sigma Prime review (2019) is of the EVM wallet (CoreWallet + WalletFactory, see dapperlabs/dapper-contracts), not of a Cadence/Flow contract; the corpus 'Flow' label therefore has no matching in-scope artifact. Dapper's Flow-side wallet contracts are deployed under a Dapper-controlled Flow account that is not published in docs, the review, or the repo. No Flow account/contract address recoverable -> PARTIAL.
